analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head lines 1028-1040). It describes a new `Traffic:` line in `darkbloom status` that reports whether the coordinator can route work to the connection. No source code, protocol, authorization, key custody or cache behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant reading:
- The text says the `Traffic:` diagnostic reports App Attest lease or legacy verification as eligibility. It is local, read-only status, and it does not grant or extend serving authorization. That is consistent with T-052, which warns against treating a label or diagnostic as permission, and with T-053/A-016, where the coordinator remains authoritative.
- The line surfaces causes such as disconnected, no verdict after 90 seconds, expired lease, locked keychain, stalled Apple call, App Attest unavailable and no linked account. This is operator-facing diagnostic text, with no secrets or token values in the described output. Its stable identity exposure is not clear from the docs (T-058). The underlying implementation in ServingReadiness.swift and StatusCommand+Traffic.swift is not supplied, so I could not verify that it does not leak identifiers or tokens. I note this as a limit rather than a finding.
- The text says Traffic is omitted while a drain or add-on hold is shown, which matches the TB-012/T-059 add-on hold documentation elsewhere in the file.
- The remaining text in the file units (logout, stop/restart, add-on, model cache) is unchanged context. I found no new regression there and did not re-raise pre-existing issues.

Remaining questions for integration: whether the code that implements the `Traffic:` line matches this documentation, and whether it avoids logging sensitive coordinator reasons. Neither is contradicted by the supplied evidence.
